Wells County Treasurer’s Office
SERVICES & DUTIES:
Maintains the County’s bank accounts and investments
Billing and collection of real and personal property taxes
Issues permits to move mobile homes or transfer titles
Pursues collections of delinquent property taxes
Conducts annual tax sale
Property tax clearance schedule (Alcohol)
Tax Payment Methods
Pay by Mail:
We accept personal checks, certified checks, and money orders. Make checks payable to the Treasurer, Wells County. Mail must be postmarked by the due date. Returned, delayed, lost, or misdirected mail may become delinquent. Please ensure the mailing address is complete and accurate, obtain proof of mailing date, and use the correct amount of postage.
Mail your payment to:
Wells County Treasurer
102 W. Market St., Suite 204
Bluffton, IN 46714
Pay at the Treasurer’s Office:
Office hours are 8 am – 4:30 pm, Monday through Friday. The office is closed to observe legal holidays. We accept checks, cash, cashier’s check, and money orders. Make checks payable to the Treasurer, Wells County. Credit/debit card payments are accepted in the office but can be made on-line or by phone. (See instructions below.)
Pay at a Bank:
The following local banks accept payments: First Bank of Berne, Farmers & Merchants State Bank & 1st Source Bank.
You will need to provide your Tax Statement along with your payment. Bank locations outside of the County do not accept payment for County taxes. Banks are not allowed to accept payments after the official deadline.
Pay Online:
To make a credit or debit card payment online, Click Here . There is a 2% fee for credit card service, and a flat fee of $4.00 for debit card. Please print or record your transaction number for future reference.
To make an electronic check payment online, Click Here . A $1.75 flat rate will be added.
Use our EscrowCheck tool to see the real-time tax payment status from banks, mortgage companies, and other lenders. Before making a payment or calling our office with questions on payment statuses, please utilize the tool below to determine if you already have an escrow on your property and whether your escrow payment has been submitted to our office.

Innkeeper's Tax
What is Wells County Innkeeper’s Tax?
On December 6, 2022, the Wells County Council approved Ordinance No. 2022-25 , which requires those engaged in the business of renting or furnishing accommodations to charge their patrons a 5% innkeeper’s tax.
Who is required to collect and pay innkeepers tax?
The innkeeper’s tax is imposed on accommodations that are rented for stays in Wells County that are less than 30 days. The tax is collected by a retail merchant (i.e., the innkeeper) from the patron (customer). The retail merchant then forwards the tax it has collected to the Wells County Treasurer on a monthly basis. To read the introduction letter to Wells County Innkeeper’s Tax, Click Here.
How do I pay Wells County Innkeeper’s Tax?
Wells County Innkeeper’s Tax returns and remittances are required to be filed with and paid to the Wells County Treasurer.
Payment may be mailed to the Wells County Treasurer’s Office at 102 W. Market St., Ste. 204, Bluffton, IN 46714. You may also make your payment in person at the same address. All payments MUST include an innkeeper's tax return form. Click Here
When is Wells County Innkeeper’s Tax due?
Payment of the innkeeper’s tax must be made on or before the 20th of each month. For example, tax collected during the month of January is due on February 20th.
How do marketplace facilitator’s pay innkeepers tax?
A marketplace facilitator (such as an online travel company) is required to collect and remit the Wells County Innkeeper’s Tax to the Indiana Department of Revenue. The DOR will then distribute the money to Wells County. Additional information regarding marketplace facilitators can be found in the Indiana Department of Revenue's Indiana County Innkeeper's Tax Guide. Click Here
